name: Nepal

facts.religion: Hindu about 81%, Buddhist about 8%, Muslim about 5%

snapshot: Six months after Gen Z protests burned parliament, a party founded in 2022 won a landslide and made a 35-year-old former rapper prime minister.
culture: Nepal is home to eight of the world's ten highest mountains, including Everest, and the Sherpa people are famed as climbers. Kathmandu valley's Hindu and Buddhist temples sit side by side, and the Kumari, a young girl worshipped as a living goddess, is a unique tradition. Dashain and Tihar are the biggest festivals. Lumbini is the birthplace of the Buddha.
society: Nepal abolished its monarchy in 2008 after a Maoist insurgency. Remittances from millions working in the Gulf, Malaysia and India make up about a quarter of GDP. Old party leaders rotated in power for years, fuelling the anger that exploded in September 2025 after a social media ban.

story: In September 2025, Nepal's government banned two dozen social media platforms. Young people, already furious at corruption and at politicians' children flaunting luxury on Instagram, poured into the streets. Police opened fire; parliament and politicians' homes were set ablaze, more than 70 people died, and Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli resigned. Six months later, the generation that brought him down picked his replacement.

In the 5 March election, the Rastriya Swatantra Party, founded only in 2022, won 182 of 275 seats, and its candidate for prime minister was Balendra "Balen" Shah, a 35-year-old structural engineer and former underground rapper whose lyrics attacked corruption, and who was elected mayor of Kathmandu as an independent in 2022 (Drishti IAS). He chose to run against Oli himself in Oli's home seat, Jhapa-5, and beat him by 49,614 votes, the largest margin in Nepal's parliamentary history (Asia News Network). Sworn in in late March, Balen became the youngest prime minister in Nepal's history and its first from the Madhesi community of the southern plains, long marginalised by hill elites. The challenges are immediate: the RSP has promised 7 percent annual growth in one of Asia's poorer countries, his party chief faces legal charges, and critics have already questioned the luxury Land Rover he campaigned in (ISAS). Nepal is now testing whether a protest movement can govern.
briefing.power: A federal parliamentary republic since the monarchy was abolished in 2008. The prime minister leads the majority in the 275-seat House of Representatives, elected by a mix of constituencies and proportional lists; the president is largely ceremonial.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Balendra Shah (RSP), in office since March 2026.
